name: Calculating Body Mass Index (BMI)
description:
BMI is a measure of body fat based on height and weight that applies to adult men and women. BMI Categories are as follows:
Underweight = <18.5
Normal weight = 18.5–24.9
Overweight = 25–29.9
Obesity = BMI of 30 or greater.
English BMI Formula (Imperial) is: BMI = (Weight in Pounds / (Height in inches x Height in inches)) x 703.
Construct a program that calculates the Body Mass Index (BMI) according to this formula.

comments.content: We need to read and process the values that the user enters. To read the input values from the user, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.
We prompt the user to enter the weight in pounds.
We need to read the weight that the user enters and store it in a variable. We read the weight by calling the nextDouble() method because weight could have a decimal point.
Note that this can only be done if user input could be translated into a valid double value.
We prompt the user to enter the height in inches.
We need to read the height that the user enters and store it in a variable. We read the height by calling the nextDouble() method because height could have a decimal point.
Note that this can only be done if user input could be translated into a valid double value.
We close the scanner as we do not want to process any input from the user in the rest of the program.
We calculate the BMI using the mathematical expression in this statement. This expression returns a floating-point number; thus, we assign its result to a variable of type double.
Math.pow(height, 2) returns the value of the first argument (height) raised to the power of the second argument (2).

We need to declare variable bmi of type double because the division returns a floating-point number (as both of its operands are double) and when one operand of multiplication operator is double, the result of multiplication would be double.

Note that the multiplication (*) and division operator (/) are in the same precedence level, and thus, are evaluated from left to right in this expression. Therefore, we don't need to include parantheses around the division.
This statement prints to the default standard output stream the text "The BMI is: " and the value of variable bmi. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
The expression in the argument of the println method returns a string that is obtained by concatenating the given string and value of the variable.
